### iliad-146 (23.287–372)

| Greek | `l` | `i` | avoided on purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| ὣς φάτο Πηλεΐδης, ταχέες δ’ ἱππῆες ἄγερθεν (23.287) | "So spoke Peleus’-son, and the swift horsemen gathered." | "So spoke the son of Peleus, and the swift horsemen gathered." | "assembled", "the swift riders"; ἱππῆες "horsemen" and Πηλεΐδης as the patronymic "Peleus’-son" follow the table |
| ὦρτο … ἄναξ ἀνδρῶν Εὔμηλος (23.288) | "Rose by far the first the lord of men, Eumelus," | "By far the first to rise was the lord of men, Eumelus," | the line of iliad-042 (Ἀγαμέμνων) with the name changed; "lord of men" kept |
| τῷ δ’ ἐπί / τῷ δ’ ἄρ’ ἐπ’ … ὦρτο (23.290, 23.293) | "and after him rose" | "and after him rose" | "upon him", "next to him"; 23.290 is the iliad-042 line with the English of that unit |
| ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἤγαγεν · ὕπαγε ζυγόν · ὑπὸ ζυγὸν ἦγε (23.291, 23.294, 23.300) | "led under the yoke" | "put under the yoke" · "bringing under the yoke" | "harnessed", "hitched"; ὑπό "under" kept visible (tmesis at 23.294) |
| Αἴθη · Πόδαργος (23.295) | "Aethe" · "Podargus" | same | "Aithe", "Podargos"; familiar Latin forms as for other proper names; Αἴθην τὴν Ἀγαμεμνονέην "Agamemnon’s mare Aethe" |
| Ἀγχισιάδης (23.296) | "Anchises’-son" | "son of Anchises" | "Anchisiades"; the patronymic as for Ἀτρεΐδης, Νεστορίδης |
| εὐρυχόρῳ Σικυῶνι (23.299) | "Sicyon of wide dancing-grounds" | "spacious Sicyon" | Odyssey table's εὐρύχορος, unchanged |
| ἐΰτριχας ὁπλίσαθ’ ἵππους (23.301, 23.351) | "made ready well-maned horses" | "made ready his well-maned horses" | "harnessed", "armed"; ἐΰτριχας "well-maned" as in iliad-143 (23.13), ὁπλίζω "make ready" as at 7.417 and 11.641 |
| ἀγλαὸς υἱὸς ὑπερθύμοιο ἄνακτος (Νέστορος, 23.302) | "the splendid son of Nestor, the high-spirited lord" | "the splendid son of Nestor, the high-spirited lord" | "proud", "great-hearted" (μεγάθυμος); ἀγλαὸς υἱός "splendid son" and ὑπέρθυμος "high-spirited" follow the table |
| Πυλοιγενέες (ἵπποι, 23.303) | "Pylos-born" | "born at Pylos" | "Pylian"; as the table row 2.54 |
| εἰς ἀγαθὰ φρονέων νοέοντι καὶ αὐτῷ (23.305) | "with good in mind, to him who also himself had understanding" | "with kindly intent, though he had understanding himself" | "wishing him well"; not a formula repeated in this part |
| βάρδιστοι θείειν (23.310) | "slowest to run" | "the slowest runners" | "the slowest to run" kept in `l` only; θείειν is the epic infinitive of θέω |
| μῆτις (μήτι, μῆτιν, 23.313, 23.315–318) | "cunning" ("by cunning") | "cunning" ("by cunning") | "counsel", "skill", "craft"; follows the table's μῆτις "cunning" (2.169) |
| ἐλατῆρες (23.369) | "drivers" | "drivers" | "charioteers" (kept for ἡνίοχος), "riders"; ἐλατήρ from ἐλαύνω |
| ἱμᾶσιν (βοέοισιν ἱμᾶσιν, 23.324; πέπληγον ἱμᾶσιν, 23.363) | "oxhide straps" · "straps" | same | "thongs" (turned down at 8.544, 22.397), "reins" (kept for ἡνία), "whips" (kept for μάστιγες); ἱμάς "strap", as the table |
| νύσσα (23.332, 23.338, 23.344) | "turning-point" | "turning-point" | "turning-post" (kept for τέρμα, which the table has at 22.162); same place, two words |
| τέρμα (23.309, 23.323, 23.333, 23.358) | "turning-post" | "turning-post" | table row τέρματα (22.162), unchanged |
| ἅρμα · ἅρματα · δίφρος (e.g. 23.334, 23.335, 23.341, 23.352, 23.368) | "chariot" | "chariot" | "car", "carriage"; plural ἅρματα for one chariot kept as the plural only where many drivers are meant (23.368) |
| κρείων Εὔμηλος (23.354) | "lord Eumelus" | "lord Eumelus" | "king"; κρείων "lord" as in the table |
| δουρὶ κλειτός (Μενέλαος, 23.355) | "famed for the spear" | "famed for his spear" | "spear-famed"; follows the table's δουρικλειτός (5.55) |
| λάχ’ ἐλαυνέμεν (23.356, 23.357) | "got by lot to drive" | "drew his place to drive" | "was chosen", "won the right to"; λαγχάνω "obtain by lot" |
| ὄχ’ ἄριστος ἐών (23.357) | "by far the best being" | "though by far the best" | table's ὄχ’ ἄριστος "by far the best" (2.761) |
| Νέστωρ Νηλήϊος (23.349) | "Nestor the Neleian" | "Nestor, son of Neleus" | "Neleian Nestor"; the adjective as in Νηλήϊαι ἵπποι (11.597, "Neleian horses"), turned into the patronymic sense in `i` |
| ἐπεὶ ᾧ παιδὶ ἑκάστου πείρατ’ ἔειπε (23.350) | "since to his own son the limits of each thing he had told" | "having told his son the limits of every point" | "the details", "the ends"; πείρατα "limits" as in πείρατα νίκης (7.101) |
| ὡς μεμνέῳτο δρόμους καὶ ἀληθείην ἀποείποι (23.361) | "so that he might remember the runs and report the truth" | "so that he would remember the runs and report the truth" | "tell the whole truth"; ἀποείπω "report", δρόμοι "runs" |
| ὁμόκλησάν τ’ ἐπέεσσιν / ἐσσυμένως (23.363–364) | "shouted at them with words eagerly" | "shouted at them with words, eagerly" | "hurriedly" (the table's 3.84 sense); "eagerly" as in 15.698; ὁμοκλάω "shout at" per the table |
| ἅμα πάντες … μάστιγας ἄειραν (23.362) | "all together raised the whips" | "all together raised their whips" | "lifted", "swung"; μάστιξ "whip" as in 5.840 |
| κονίη ἵστατ’ ἀειρομένη ὥς τε νέφος ἠὲ θύελλα (23.365–366) | "the dust stood up, rising, like a cloud or a storm-blast" | "the dust rose and stood in the air like a cloud or a storm-blast" | table's κονίη ἵστατ’ ἀειρομένη (2.150–151); θύελλα "storm-blast" (Odyssey 5.304) |
| ἀΐξασκε μετήορα (23.369) | "darted up, hanging in the air" | "darted up and hung in the air" | "leapt" (turned down for ἀΐσσω); the iterative -σκε is explained in the note; μετήορα as at 8.26 |
| Departure from the Odyssey: σῆμα δέ τοι ἐρέω μάλ’ ἀριφραδές, οὐδέ σε λήσει (23.326) | "And a sign to you I will tell, very plain, and it will not escape you." | "And I will tell you a sign, very plain, that will not escape you." | the Odyssey (odyssey-052) wording with the colon changed to the edition's full stop here; the validator may warn, the wording is otherwise unchanged |
